schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE EMPLOYEE (
    EMPID INT,
    NAME VARCHAR(255),
    SUPERVISOR INT,
    SALARY INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (EMPID),
    CHECK (EMPID <> SUPERVISOR),
    CHECK (SALARY >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE BONUS (
    EMPID INT,
    BONUS INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (EMPID),
    FOREIGN KEY (EMPID) REFERENCES EMPLOYEE(EMPID),
    CHECK (BONUS >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE BONUS < 1000 OR BONUS IS NULL
q2: SELECT NAME, BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS USING(EMPID) WHERE BONUS <1000 OR BONUS IS NULL

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because of the difference in how the LEFT JOIN is specified. Q1 uses the ON clause to join EMPLOYEE and BONUS, while Q2 uses the USING clause. The USING clause in Q2 will join on all columns with the same name in both tables, which in this case is EMPID. This can lead to different results if there are multiple columns with the same name in the tables being joined.
counterexample_dsp: The difference in results will be triggered when there are multiple columns with the same name in the EMPLOYEE and BONUS tables. In this case, the difference will be in the number of rows returned by the two queries.
